name: created-then-removed-assertion-scope
body: Four limits. (1) The save's `no pending changes` report is written to the coordinator process's stdout while the client reply is the fixed `Session saved`, so the no-op is pinned by durable state (no node file, no commit, empty ledger, no dirty row, absent read), not by wording; upgrade if the message itself must ever be pinned — capture the session process's stdout — but the test should stay state-based even then. (2) The "no dirty row" read is scoped to the `Requirement` table, the only table the create-then-remove fixture touches; widen it if a later task makes the test admit mutations on more than one node table. (3) `Coordinator::save` derives its delete set from the pending-removal ledger alone, and both arms assert the post-save `PendingRemoval` count is zero ("save must leave no ledger identity for the re-added node"), so the drain is pinned; a new arm must keep that post-save zero assertion. (4) The no-op save is pinned by a whole-run occurrence count of the coordinator's `Session saved: no pending changes` line, so an arm adding another empty-pending-set save must raise that count.
